items.meaning: no more rooms, tables, or tickets are available.
items.example: Unfortunately, the hotel is fully booked for the dates you requested.
items.plain: Unfortunately, the hotel has no rooms left for the dates you requested.
items.note: A common response when trying to reserve something popular.

items.meaning: to register your arrival at a hotel or airport.
items.example: We need to check in at least two hours before our flight departs.
items.plain: We need to register our arrival at least two hours before our flight departs.

items.meaning: to pay your bill and leave a hotel.
items.example: What time do we need to check out of the hotel tomorrow morning?
items.plain: When do we need to leave the hotel tomorrow morning after paying?

items.meaning: not working correctly or broken.
items.example: The elevator is out of order, so we'll have to use the stairs.
items.plain: The elevator is broken, so we'll have to use the stairs.
items.note: Common sign or announcement for broken equipment.

items.meaning: to leave a bus, train, or other public transport at a specific stop.
items.example: You need to get off at the third stop after the bridge.
items.plain: You need to leave the bus at the third stop after the bridge.
items.note: Essential for giving/receiving directions on public transport.

items.meaning: to board a bus, train, or other public transport.
items.example: You should get on the number 14 bus to reach the city centre.
items.plain: You should board the number 14 bus to reach the city centre.
items.note: Essential for giving/receiving directions on public transport.

items.meaning: to investigate or examine a problem.
items.example: The hotel manager said he would look into it and get back to us.
items.plain: The hotel manager said he would investigate the problem and get back to us.
items.note: Common response when someone promises to address a problem.

items.text: point me in the direction of
items.form: point me in the direction of
items.meaning: to show someone where something is.
items.example: Could you please point me in the direction of the nearest ATM?
items.plain: Could you please show me where the nearest ATM is?
items.note: Polite way to ask for directions.

items.meaning: walking rather than using transport.
items.example: The museum is only ten minutes away if you go on foot.
items.plain: The museum is only ten minutes away if you walk.
items.note: Common way to describe walking distance.

items.meaning: using a bus as a mode of transport.
items.example: We decided to go by bus to save money on taxis.
items.plain: We decided to use the bus to save money on taxis.
items.note: Common way to specify transport method.

items.meaning: using a train as a mode of transport.
items.example: It's quicker to get there by train than by car during peak hours.
items.plain: It's quicker to use the train than a car during peak hours.
items.note: Common way to specify transport method.

items.meaning: using a taxi as a mode of transport.
items.example: We'll go by taxi directly to the airport to avoid any delays.
items.plain: We'll use a taxi directly to the airport to avoid any delays.
items.note: Common way to specify transport method.

items.meaning: located to the left side.
items.example: The entrance to the park is just past the fountain, on the left.
items.plain: The entrance to the park is just past the fountain, to the left side.

items.meaning: located to the right side.
items.example: You'll see the hotel sign on the right after you turn the corner.
items.plain: You'll see the hotel sign to the right after you turn the corner.

items.meaning: directly forward without turning.
items.example: Just keep walking straight ahead for about five minutes, and you'll see it.
items.plain: Just keep walking directly forward for about five minutes, and you'll see it.

items.meaning: to change direction to the left.
items.example: At the next intersection, you need to turn left towards the river.
items.plain: At the next intersection, you need to go left towards the river.

items.meaning: to change direction to the right.
items.example: After the bakery, turn right, and the museum will be on your left.
items.plain: After the bakery, go right, and the museum will be on your left.

items.meaning: located at the intersection of two streets.
items.example: The cafe you're looking for is right on the corner of Main Street and Elm Avenue.
items.plain: The cafe you're looking for is at the intersection of Main Street and Elm Avenue.

items.meaning: a very short distance away.
items.example: Don't worry, the train station is just around the corner from here.
items.plain: Don't worry, the train station is very close to here.

items.meaning: a short distance, typically in a city grid.
items.example: The art gallery is just a few blocks away, an easy walk.
items.plain: The art gallery is a short distance away, an easy walk.
items.note: Common for describing distance in urban areas.

items.meaning: to arrive at the scheduled moment.
items.example: We left early to make it on time for our train departure.
items.plain: We left early to arrive at the scheduled moment for our train departure.

items.meaning: to be delayed and behind schedule.
items.example: Our flight is running late due to unexpected weather conditions.
items.plain: Our flight is delayed due to unexpected weather conditions.

items.meaning: happening at the planned time.
items.example: Good news, our train is running perfectly on schedule.
items.plain: Good news, our train is running exactly at the planned time.

items.meaning: happening later than planned.
items.example: Unfortunately, the bus is running behind schedule by about 20 minutes.
items.plain: Unfortunately, the bus is running later than planned by about 20 minutes.

items.meaning: an instruction to put your signature on a document.
items.example: Please sign here to confirm you've received your rental car keys.
items.plain: Please put your signature here to confirm you've received your rental car keys.

items.meaning: asking for the scheduled hour of an event or service.
items.example: What time is the last train to Edinburgh tonight?
items.plain: When does the last train to Edinburgh leave tonight?

items.meaning: asking for the price of something.
items.example: How much does it cost to get a taxi from the airport to the city centre?
items.plain: What is the price of a taxi from the airport to the city centre?
items.note: Direct and common way to ask about prices.

items.meaning: to state that something is not working or is incorrect.
items.example: There's a problem with the heating in our room; it's not working.
items.plain: The heating in our room isn't working; it's not functioning.
items.note: Direct and common way to report an issue.

items.meaning: to express dissatisfaction with a service or product.
items.example: I'd like to complain about the noise from the room next door.
items.plain: I want to express my dissatisfaction with the noise from the room next door.
items.note: Polite but firm way to make a complaint.

items.meaning: to indicate that an item or situation is faulty or incorrect.
items.example: Something is wrong with the Wi-Fi connection; I can't get online.
items.plain: The Wi-Fi connection is faulty; I can't get online.
items.note: General way to report a malfunction.

items.meaning: polite way to ask for information.
items.example: Could you tell me how to get to the nearest post office?
items.plain: Please inform me how to get to the nearest post office.
items.note: Very common and polite way to ask questions.

items.meaning: to state what you are trying to find.
items.example: I'm looking for a good coffee shop with free Wi-Fi nearby.
items.plain: I want to find a good coffee shop with free Wi-Fi nearby.
items.note: Common way to ask for directions or recommendations.

items.meaning: polite way to ask for specific information.
items.example: Do you know if this bus goes to the city centre?
items.plain: Can you tell me if this bus goes to the city centre?

items.meaning: asking for the location of something.
items.example: Excuse me, where can I find the departure lounge for international flights?
items.plain: Excuse me, where is the departure lounge for international flights?
items.note: Direct way to ask for a location.

items.meaning: asking for directions to a place.
items.example: Excuse me, how do I get to the main square from here?
items.plain: Excuse me, what's the way to the main square from here?

items.meaning: polite way to ask for assistance.
items.example: Excuse me, could you help me with my luggage up these stairs?
items.plain: Excuse me, would you assist me with my luggage up these stairs?

items.meaning: to state that you require help with a specific task.
items.example: I need assistance with checking in my oversized baggage.
items.plain: I require help with checking in my oversized baggage.
items.note: Slightly more formal than 'could you help me'.

items.meaning: asking for the most efficient or suitable method.
items.example: What's the best way to get to the airport at this time of day?
items.plain: What is the most efficient method to get to the airport now?
items.note: Common for seeking advice on routes or methods.

items.meaning: asking if a reduced price is available.
items.example: Is there a discount for students or seniors on this tour?
items.plain: Do you offer a reduced price for students or seniors on this tour?
items.note: Polite way to inquire about special rates.

items.meaning: asking if a particular payment method is valid.
items.example: Do you accept credit cards, or is it cash only for this purchase?
items.plain: Can I pay with a credit card, or do I need cash for this purchase?
items.note: Common when asking about payment options.

items.meaning: to book a place or service in advance.
items.example: I called the restaurant to make a reservation for two for Friday evening.
items.plain: I called the restaurant to book a table for two for Friday evening.
items.note: Standard for booking tables, rooms, or tickets.

items.meaning: to find out if something is free or can be used.
items.example: Could you please check availability for a double room next week?
items.plain: Could you please see if a double room is free next week?
items.note: Common when booking hotels or services.

items.meaning: to verify that a reservation is still valid.
items.example: I'd like to confirm the booking I made online for next Tuesday.
items.plain: I'd like to verify the reservation I made online for next Tuesday.
items.note: Essential for peace of mind before travel.

items.meaning: to call off a booking.
items.example: I need to cancel a reservation I made for tomorrow night.
items.plain: I need to call off the booking I made for tomorrow night.
items.note: Standard phrase for cancelling any booking.

items.meaning: a document allowing you to board a plane or ship.
items.example: Please have your boarding pass and passport ready at the gate.
items.plain: Please have your ticket and passport ready at the gate.

items.meaning: the area in an airport where you collect your luggage.
items.example: After landing, we headed straight to baggage claim to pick up our suitcases.
items.plain: After landing, we went directly to the area where you collect luggage.

items.meaning: a second flight taken to reach your final destination.
items.example: Our connecting flight to Rome departs from Gate B12 in an hour.
items.plain: Our next flight to Rome leaves from Gate B12 in an hour.

items.meaning: the specific exit point for boarding a flight.
items.example: Please proceed to your departure gate as boarding will begin shortly.
items.plain: Please go to your specific exit point for boarding as it starts soon.

items.meaning: food and drink delivered to your hotel room.
items.example: I'll order room service for dinner tonight; I'm too tired to go out.
items.plain: I'll have dinner delivered to my hotel room tonight; I'm too tired.

items.meaning: a free breakfast provided by the hotel.
items.example: Our stay includes a complimentary breakfast served in the dining room.
items.plain: Our stay includes a free breakfast served in the dining room.

items.meaning: the reception area of a hotel.
items.example: Please report any issues with your room to the front desk.
items.plain: Please report any issues with your room to the reception area.
items.note: Main point of contact in a hotel.

items.meaning: buses, trains, and subways available to everyone.
items.example: Is it easy to get around the city using public transport?
items.plain: Is it easy to get around the city using buses, trains, and subways?

items.meaning: a designated place where taxis wait for passengers.
items.example: You can find a taxi stand just outside the main entrance of the station.
items.plain: You can find a place where taxis wait just outside the main entrance.

items.meaning: a place where a bus regularly stops to pick up or drop off passengers.
items.example: Which bus stop should I use to get to the museum from here?
items.plain: Where does the bus stop that goes to the museum from here?

items.meaning: a place where trains stop for passengers.
items.example: How far is the nearest train station from our hotel?
items.plain: How far is the nearest place where trains stop from our hotel?

items.meaning: a car you hire for a period of time.
items.example: We decided to get a rental car to explore the countryside at our own pace.
items.plain: We decided to hire a car to explore the countryside at our own pace.

items.meaning: a ticket for a journey to a destination but not back.
items.example: I'd like to buy a one way ticket to London for tomorrow morning.
items.plain: I'd like to buy a ticket to London for tomorrow morning, but not back.

items.meaning: a ticket for a journey to a destination and back again.
items.example: Could I get a return ticket to the city centre, please?
items.plain: Could I get a ticket to the city centre and back, please?

items.meaning: the busiest time for travel, usually morning and evening.
items.example: Try to avoid travelling during rush hour if you want to miss the crowds.
items.plain: Try to avoid travelling during the busiest time if you want to miss the crowds.
items.note: Important for planning travel in cities.

items.meaning: a long line of vehicles that cannot move or move very slowly.
items.example: We got stuck in a huge traffic jam on the way to the airport.
items.plain: We got stuck in a huge line of unmoving cars on the way to the airport.

items.meaning: to switch from one train to another to continue a journey.
items.example: We need to change trains at the next station to get to our destination.
items.plain: We need to switch from one train to another at the next station.

items.meaning: to no longer have one's passport, usually by misplacing it.
items.example: I've lost my passport and need to report it to the embassy.
items.plain: My passport is missing and I need to report it to the embassy.

items.meaning: bags that have not arrived at the destination with the passenger.
items.example: I need to report some missing luggage from my flight from Dublin.
items.plain: I need to report that my bags didn't arrive from my flight from Dublin.

items.meaning: to charge someone too much money for something.
items.example: I think the taxi driver overcharged me for the ride to the hotel.
items.plain: I think the taxi driver charged me too much for the ride to the hotel.

items.meaning: to receive money back for a product or service.
items.example: I'd like to get a refund for the tour that was cancelled.
items.plain: I'd like to receive my money back for the tour that was cancelled.

items.meaning: to resolve a problem or difficulty.
items.example: Could you please help me sort out the issue with my booking?
items.plain: Could you please help me resolve the problem with my booking?
items.note: Common way to ask for problem resolution.

items.meaning: the money used in a particular country.
items.example: Do you know where I can exchange my money for local currency?
items.plain: Do you know where I can exchange my money for the country's money?

items.meaning: the value of one currency in relation to another.
items.example: What's the current exchange rate for euros to US dollars?
items.plain: What is the current value of euros compared to US dollars?

items.meaning: a place providing advice and maps for visitors.
items.example: We should visit the tourist information centre for maps and local tips.
items.plain: We should visit the place that gives advice and maps for visitors.

items.meaning: the times a business or attraction is open.
items.example: What are the opening hours for the museum on weekends?
items.plain: When is the museum open on weekends?

items.meaning: the money you pay to enter a place.
items.example: Is there an entrance fee to get into the botanical gardens?
items.plain: Do I have to pay money to get into the botanical gardens?

items.meaning: internet access available without charge.
items.example: Does this cafe offer free Wi-Fi for customers?
items.plain: Does this cafe offer internet access without charge for customers?

items.meaning: insurance that covers losses and medical expenses while travelling.
items.example: Make sure you have good travel insurance before you leave for your trip.
items.plain: Make sure you have insurance for your trip before you leave.

items.meaning: a person to be notified in case of an emergency.
items.example: Please provide an emergency contact number when filling out this form.
items.plain: Please provide a number for someone to call in an emergency.

items.meaning: a place where lost items are kept.
items.example: I left my umbrella on the train; I'll check the lost and found.
items.plain: I left my umbrella on the train; I'll check the place for lost items.

items.meaning: the current time in a specific geographical area.
items.example: What's the local time in Tokyo right now?
items.plain: What is the current time in Tokyo right now?
items.note: Important for communication across time zones.

items.meaning: the variation in time between two places.
items.example: There's a six-hour time difference between here and my home country.
items.plain: There's a six-hour variation in time between here and my home country.

items.meaning: the service of converting one country's money into another's.
items.example: Is there a currency exchange office at the airport?
items.plain: Is there a place to convert money at the airport?

items.meaning: a device that allows electronic devices to be used in different countries.
items.example: Don't forget to pack a travel adapter for your phone charger.
items.plain: Don't forget to pack a device for your phone charger to use abroad.

items.meaning: a designated location where someone or something is collected.
items.example: The shuttle bus has a designated pick up point outside the terminal.
items.plain: The shuttle bus has a designated place to collect passengers outside the terminal.
items.note: Common for tours, taxis, or shuttles.

items.meaning: a designated location where someone or something is left.
items.example: The taxi driver will take us directly to the drop off point at the hotel entrance.
items.plain: The taxi driver will take us directly to the place where we get out at the hotel entrance.

items.meaning: to walk from one side of a road to the other.
items.example: You'll need to cross the street at the traffic lights to reach the park.
items.plain: You'll need to walk to the other side of the street at the traffic lights.

items.meaning: to use the underground train system.
items.example: It's faster to take the subway to the museum during peak traffic.
items.plain: It's faster to use the underground train system to the museum during peak traffic.

items.meaning: to use a bus for transportation.
items.example: We can take a bus from the hotel directly to the beach.
items.plain: We can use a bus from the hotel directly to the beach.

items.meaning: to use a taxi for transportation.
items.example: It's late, so let's take a taxi back to the apartment.
items.plain: It's late, so let's use a taxi back to the apartment.

items.meaning: to get on a train to travel.
items.example: We need to hurry if we want to catch a train before midnight.
items.plain: We need to hurry if we want to get on a train before midnight.

items.meaning: to fail to board a plane at the scheduled time.
items.example: I hope we don't miss a flight because of this traffic.
items.plain: I hope we don't fail to board our plane because of this traffic.

items.meaning: to complete a document with required information.
items.example: You'll need to fill out a form at the reception desk for your check-in.
items.plain: You'll need to complete a document at the reception desk for your check-in.

items.meaning: the area where passports are checked when entering or leaving a country.
items.example: We spent a long time waiting at passport control after our international flight.
items.plain: We spent a long time waiting where passports are checked after our international flight.

items.meaning: an inspection to ensure safety, especially at airports.
items.example: All passengers must go through a security check before boarding.
items.plain: All passengers must go through an inspection for safety before boarding.

items.meaning: a store at an airport or port where goods are sold without tax.
items.example: I'll buy some souvenirs at the duty-free shop before my flight.
items.plain: I'll buy some souvenirs at the tax-free shop before my flight.

items.meaning: a book or person that provides information about a place for tourists.
items.example: We bought a travel guide to help us plan our itinerary for the trip.
items.plain: We bought a book with information about the place to plan our itinerary.

items.meaning: a map showing the streets and features of a city.
items.example: Do you have a free city map available at the reception?
items.plain: Do you have a free map of the city available at the reception?
items.note: Essential for navigating a new city.

items.meaning: a place of interest for tourists.
items.example: The Eiffel Tower is a famous tourist attraction in Paris.
items.plain: The Eiffel Tower is a famous place of interest for tourists in Paris.

items.meaning: the traditional food of a particular region or country.
items.example: We're excited to try the local cuisine during our trip to Italy.
items.plain: We're excited to try the traditional food of the region during our trip to Italy.

items.meaning: a store selling items kept as a reminder of a place.
items.example: Let's stop at that souvenir shop to buy gifts for our family.
items.plain: Let's stop at that store selling items to remember the place.

items.meaning: a machine that dispenses money; an ATM.
items.example: Is there a cash machine inside the airport terminal?
items.plain: Is there an ATM inside the airport terminal?

items.meaning: a plastic card used to make purchases on credit.
items.example: Do you accept credit card payments here, or is it cash only?
items.plain: Do you accept plastic card payments here, or is it cash only?

items.meaning: a business that helps people plan and book trips.
items.example: We booked our entire holiday through a local travel agency.
items.plain: We booked our entire holiday through a local business that plans trips.

items.meaning: a detailed plan for a journey, including routes and times.
items.example: Our travel itinerary includes visits to three different cities.
items.plain: Our detailed plan for the journey includes visits to three different cities.

items.meaning: the employees who work at a hotel.
items.example: The hotel staff were very helpful when we had a problem with our room.
items.plain: The employees who work at the hotel were very helpful when we had a problem.

items.meaning: the main counter in a hotel or office where visitors are greeted.
items.example: You can pick up your keys at the reception desk upon arrival.
items.plain: You can pick up your keys at the main counter upon arrival.
items.note: Primary point of contact in a hotel.

items.meaning: the key or card that opens a hotel room.
items.example: I seem to have lost my room key; could I get a replacement?
items.plain: I seem to have lost the key to my room; could I get a replacement?

items.meaning: a bus that travels regularly between two places.
items.example: There's a free shuttle bus from the airport to the hotel every 30 minutes.
items.plain: There's a free bus that travels regularly from the airport to the hotel.

items.meaning: the amount of luggage a passenger is permitted to carry.
items.example: Check your baggage allowance carefully to avoid extra fees.
items.plain: Check the amount of luggage you can carry carefully to avoid extra fees.

items.meaning: small bags that passengers are allowed to carry onto an aircraft.
items.example: Make sure your hand luggage fits the airline's size restrictions.
items.plain: Make sure your small bags you carry onto the plane fit the size restrictions.

items.meaning: luggage that is put in the hold of an aircraft.
items.example: We only have one piece of checked luggage for our entire trip.
items.plain: We only have one piece of luggage that goes in the plane's hold.
items.note: Luggage that is not carried into the cabin.

items.meaning: the area in an airport where passengers wait to board their flights.
items.example: We'll meet you in the departure lounge after we go through security.
items.plain: We'll meet you in the area where passengers wait to board flights.

items.meaning: the area in an airport where passengers arrive.
items.example: My family will be waiting for me in the arrival hall.
items.plain: My family will be waiting for me in the area where passengers arrive.

items.meaning: a place where you can get information, often in a public building.
items.example: If you have any questions, please ask at the information desk.
items.plain: If you have any questions, please ask at the place where you get information.

items.meaning: items that have been lost and found.
items.example: I reported my lost wallet at the lost property office at the station.
items.plain: I reported my lost wallet at the office for lost and found items.
items.note: British English for lost and found.

items.meaning: nausea and vomiting caused by motion during travel.
items.example: I always get travel sickness on long bus journeys, so I take medication.
items.plain: I always feel nauseous on long bus journeys, so I take medication.

items.meaning: extreme tiredness and other physical effects felt after a long flight across time zones.
items.example: I'm still suffering from jet lag after my flight from Australia.
items.plain: I'm still suffering from tiredness after my long flight across time zones.

items.meaning: the desk at an airport where you register for your flight.
items.example: Please proceed to the check-in counter for your flight to New York.
items.plain: Please proceed to the desk where you register for your flight to New York.

items.meaning: the point at an airport where passengers and their luggage are screened.
items.example: We need to be at the security gate at least an hour before boarding.
items.plain: We need to be at the screening point at least an hour before boarding.

items.meaning: a display showing flight or train departure times and gates.
items.example: Check the departure board for the latest information on your flight.
items.plain: Check the display showing flight departure times for the latest information.

items.meaning: a display showing flight or train arrival times.
items.example: My friend is arriving soon; I'll check the arrival board for her flight number.
items.plain: My friend is arriving soon; I'll check the display showing flight arrival times.

items.meaning: a second train taken to reach your final destination.
items.example: We have ten minutes to catch our connecting train to Manchester.
items.plain: We have ten minutes to catch our second train to Manchester.
items.note: Common for train journeys with transfers.

items.meaning: public transportation within a specific area or city.
items.example: The hotel provides excellent information about local transport options.
items.plain: The hotel provides excellent information about public transportation within the city.

items.meaning: passports, visas, tickets, and other papers needed for a trip.
items.example: Make sure you have all your travel documents ready before you leave.
items.plain: Make sure you have all your passports, visas, and tickets ready before you leave.

items.meaning: the conditions and documents needed to obtain a visa.
items.example: You should check the visa requirements for your destination country well in advance.
items.plain: You should check what you need to get a visa for your destination country.

items.meaning: an officer who checks goods entering a country.
items.example: The customs official asked me about the items in my suitcase.
items.plain: The officer who checks goods entering the country asked me about my suitcase.

items.meaning: an officer who checks people entering a country.
items.example: The immigration officer stamped my passport and welcomed me to the country.
items.plain: The officer who checks people entering the country stamped my passport.

behind schedule.note: Checker slip: The key accurately defines 'behind schedule' in the given example.
